tags.qa_notes: Re-audited 2026-08-05 (deep wreck-history cross-check). All core facts re-confirmed live: 180m/600ft length and 18,427 GRT confirmed by Wikipedia, puregrenada.com, ecodiveandtrek.com (fresh fetch). One outlier: dreamwrecks.com states 536ft rather than 600ft; 4+ other independent sources agree on 180m/600ft, so 536ft is treated as a likely error in that single source, not a genuine unresolved conflict - noted in markdown. NEW DETAIL ADDED (2+ sources - grenada-history.org and dreamwrecks.com, both fetched fresh 2026-08-05): the burning vessel was under tow by HMS Londonderry toward a reef near Pointe Salines when the towline parted in a gust of wind; she sank stern-first at noon on 24 October 1961. TIGHTENED: stern-section loss date narrowed from 'late 1980s-early 1990s' to 'late 1992', per fresh Wikipedia fetch and corroborating aggregate search, both independently landing on 1992. Three deaths (1 immediate + Second Mate died of burns 2 days later + third crewman died of burns in Caracas) re-confirmed via numa.net/grenada-history.org narrative in addition to prior Wikipedia confirmation. No hallucinations found this round; prior 2026-06-04 QA held up under re-verification.

No hallucinations found.

Re-audited 2026-08-05 - SIGNIFICANT CORRECTIONS. HALLUCINATION-ADJACENT CLAIM REMOVED: 'vehicle graveyard (cars and buses) at 90ft' - the 2026-06-04 QA attributed this to PADI and Sportif Dive, but a direct fresh fetch of padi.com/dive-site/grenada/happy-valley/ (fetched twice on 2026-08-05) explicitly contains NO mention of vehicles, cars, buses, or a graveyard, and sportifdive.co.uk/divesites/... now 404s and cannot be re-verified. The claim appears to trace only to an AI-generated WebSearch aggregation, not to any directly-fetchable primary source - removed per anti-hallucination policy. SITE IDENTITY AMBIGUITY FLAGGED: fresh fetch of turq.com shows it treats 'Valleys of the Whale' (whale-sighting naming story, ~18m/60ft, part of the Boss Reef 'Valleys' section) and 'Happy Valley' (Admiralty anchor, wall dive to 28m/90ft, drift to Dragon Bay) as two neighbouring but distinct entries - not confirmed as the same site. Our coordinates/depth/wall classification match 'Happy Valley' far more closely than 'Valleys of the Whale'. WHALE-NAMING STORY DOWNGRADED TO SINGLE-SOURCE: only turq.com attests to the whale-and-calf sighting naming origin; no second independent source could be found despite targeted search - this fails the 2-source bar for historical/naming claims and is now explicitly flagged as unconfirmed in the markdown rather than stated as fact. Admiralty anchor and wall-to-Dragon-Bay drift character remain well-supported (turq.com, live padi.com fetch, live ecodiveandtrek.com fetch - 3 sources).
